ask: Post this video of our new serum on TikTok: https://cdn.example.com/serum.mp4
before: The reply asked two things TikTok needs: who should see it, and whether it's the brand's own product or a paid partnership. The user said: public, and it's our own product, nobody paid us.

arguments.content: Three drops, thirty seconds, done. Our new serum is here.

steps.why: The decision: the video sells the brand's own product, so TikTok expects it disclosed as promoting the user's business: brand_organic_toggle. Not brand_content_toggle, which is for a paid partner. These two can only be set in platform_specific. The post's text is the caption.

Privacy through the details call, which refuses a misspelled level; in platform_specific a typo would quietly become the first level the account allows. Public is what the user said. Duets and stitches stay on: product demos spread through them.
Read back metadata.platformSpecific.tiktok for the disclosure; the privacy reply already showed the saved level.

say: Saved to Acme as a TikTok draft, public to everyone, marked as promoting your own business: "Three drops, thirty seconds, done. Our new serum is here." Duets and stitches are on. Nothing goes out yet. Schedule it?
never: Deciding for the user that a product video needs no disclosure.
Setting the disclosure with update-post-platform-details: it answers success and keeps nothing.
